---
title: "`ev_collapse()` — redundant-pathway dedup"
---

## Purpose

Collapse the many overlapping pathways that enrichment returns into a
non-redundant set, so a ring/figure shows distinct biology rather than ten names
for the same gene cluster.

## When to use

After `ev_enrich()`, before plotting. The hero function applies it automatically
via the `dedup` argument.

## How it works

Two families of **collection-agnostic** methods (they work for Hallmark,
Reactome, KEGG, MitoCarta, CORUM, GO — no GO structure required):

1. **`fgsea::collapsePathways`** — a conditional permutation independence test.
   For each significant pathway it re-runs fgsea conditioning on a candidate
   parent's genes; a pathway whose signal disappears is marked redundant. "Main
   pathways" survive.
2. **Set-similarity on leading-edge genes** — drop a pathway too similar to a
   better-ranked one. The metric is chosen with `similarity`.

The default `method = "collapse_then_jaccard"` runs (1) then (2).

### Similarity metric

| `similarity` | Formula | Catches | EnrichmentMap cutoff |
|---|---|---|---|
| `jaccard` (default) | $\frac{|A\cap B|}{|A\cup B|}$ | symmetric overlap | 0.25 |
| `overlap` | $\frac{|A\cap B|}{\min(|A|,|B|)}$ | small set ⊂ large set | 0.5 |
| `combined` | $w\cdot J + (1-w)\cdot O$ | both (Cytoscape default) | 0.375 |

`overlap` is the one to reach for when a focused signature is swamped by a broad
parent term; `combined` (with `combined_weight = w`, default 0.5) is the
Cytoscape EnrichmentMap edge metric.

::: {.callout-note}
GO-semantic collapse (`clusterProfiler::simplify`, `rrvgo`) is intentionally not
offered here: it hard-stops outside GO and needs an OrgDb. See
[methods: why GO-semantic methods are not core](../methods.qmd#dedup-survey).
:::

## Parameters & defaults

| Argument | Default | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `method` | `"collapse_then_jaccard"` | matches the source figure pipeline |
| `similarity` | `"jaccard"` | backward compatible; `overlap`/`combined` opt-in |
| `combined_weight` | `0.5` | EnrichmentMap weighting |
| `cutoff` | `0.5` | similarity threshold (set 0.375 for EM `combined`) |
| `scope` | `"within_db"` | dedup per database; `cross_db`/`global` available |
| `sig_threshold` | `0.05` | only significant pathways are deduped |
| `collapse_pval_threshold` | `0.05` | forwarded to `collapsePathways` |
| `keep_by` | `"padj"` | representative chosen by smallest FDR |

## Literature

- Korotkevich G, *et al.* "Fast gene set enrichment analysis (collapsePathways)."
  bioRxiv 2021. doi:10.1101/060012.
- Merico D, *et al.* "Enrichment Map." *PLoS One* 2010;5(11):e13984. PMID:21085593.

## Example

```r
e <- ev_enrich(dep, contrast = "CTLvMITO", databases = "reactome", species = "rat")
ev_collapse(e, method = "jaccard", similarity = "combined",
            combined_weight = 0.5, cutoff = 0.375, scope = "cross_db")
```
